Formulation
- Brief summary:
  - Patient is a 48-year-old male presenting with a 3-day history of acute vomiting (now resolved) and ongoing watery diarrhoea (~5–6 times/day) with decreased oral intake and subjective dehydration and weakness. Family history includes paternal bowel cancer and maternal type 2 diabetes. Lives alone and has been off work as a software engineer for the past few days. No mental health concerns or past psychiatric history documented. Contributing factors appear medical/physical (acute gastroenteritis); no psychiatric predisposition, precipitating or perpetuating psychological factors were documented.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem:
- (Presenting physical problem listed for context) Acute gastroenteritis with diarrhoea and probable dehydration
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Rehydrate and recover from diarrhoea; return to work when recovered
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Symptomatic improvement and prevention/treatment of dehydration; review if no improvement
- Actions (Patient):
  - Drink plenty of fluids
  - Obtain and use oral rehydration solution (Dioralyte) as advised
  - Take paracetamol if feeling feverish/weak
  - Continue time off work; remain diarrhea-free for 24–48 hours before returning to work
  - Contact clinic/return for review if not improved within one week
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Advise oral rehydration and symptomatic care
  - Recommend paracetamol for fever/weakness
  - Advise duration of work leave until 24–48 hours diarrhea-free
  - Arrange follow-up review if symptoms persist beyond one week
